intro.text: Dealings with demons, which the people of Mountaincrest fear as evil. Witches are said to keep spellbooks and to urge people to free the Megalith.

Any dealing with demons on Miral. Its practitioners are known as witches, hexers, demon keepers or Inspirers. Mountaincrest fears it, but the peoples of the southern plains practise it openly and know it best.

description.text: Witches, so people believe, are servants of evil rather than its masters. They live as outcasts, though many are rumoured to be in Kingseat.
People are quick to cry witchcraft: nearly anyone whose house burns down is called a witch, and telling of visions can bring the charge. Witches are said to promise long life or freedom from disease.
Rumour credits witches with the power to wipe out cities, eat souls and enchant people.
Captured witches are always gagged, and ordinary people are sometimes taken for witches by mistake.

The Prophet never forbade witchcraft, but warned that it was very dangerous, and opposing it matters greatly to his religion. By law witches have no protection: even those who toy with a bond face exile, prison or death, and captives are chained in rubber-coated metal.

items.text: Witchcraft began when demons came to Miral. The ancients could command demons and keep the bond far safer, though some still died. After trapping the Megalith, the Prophet warned against witchcraft, the root of Mountaincrest's laws, and many books on it passed to the church.
Some time after the Prophet disappeared, a king made a covenant letting captured witches serve him as hexers. When the Megalith was released there were nineteen of them.
Bonded to her demon, December burned through about three prison bars before her fire gave out.
Among the hexers, she chose to free her demon from their bond rather than bind it by contract.
December became the first ever to forge a bond of equals rather than of command and obedience, sharing her whole heart with a demon.
Hexers count as a kind of witch. They send messages over long distances using carrier demons.

The contracts hexers take limit their power but keep their souls from being devoured. They can make demon blood last longer before melting, though it stiffens. Some compare the king's use of them to a captain who keeps a band of brigands under control.
Hexers bond demons as other witches do, but also bind them by contract, and Kingseat relies on them.
Hexers dress in black robes and make their home in a village within the demon's chest, where they mine demonstone by heating it. A contracted demon glows dimly, like a coal.

What sets hexers apart is the king's covenant: rather than be executed, captured witches may serve the king. Society accepts them only because the king, and much of Kingseat, depends on them, and they are barely paid, slaves in all but name.

The contract is a Command, a short and plain speech. Spoken, it shrinks the demon into a marble-sized, crystal-studded ball and silences it, so it cannot tempt anyone. Every hexer must take it by the king's order. Hexers can ward against demons, though strong ones ignore wards, and cannot turn their demon fire on people.
A bond with a demon endangers body and soul. A bonded witch can start and control fire.
A witch can push the fire within out into objects, heating them or setting them alight. When a bond begins, the eyes glow faintly, and brighter as it deepens.
Heat passes easily into metal but less readily into wood. Witches do not feel the heat they pour out, and most need months of practice to melt an iron bar.

A demon wants the bond, yet by forming it gives up power over itself. A bonded pair feel a pull that keeps them near each other, and the witch's fire slowly refills. Even witches who studied all their lives have died.

The bond, called the Zuhel bond, needs both partners' consent. It grows riskier as the demon keeps tempting, and one slip can let it devour the witch's soul. Most assume the human is the weaker partner, but the reverse is true.
The stronger the demon, the deeper the well of fire it gives. Each bonded demon shows as a star-like fire in the eyes, which the demon itself can make glow, and a powerful witch can vaporize people.

Demons can also be swayed without a bond. A trained will can dominate one, holding out against pain as the soul is drained; knowing the demon well helps, and simply describing a small one may be enough. Thinking of or describing a demon can also make it more or less aggressive.

Demons feed on genuine emotion, so bargains can be struck: plains folk hurt the great walkers with silver dust and reward them with songs. Words of command can also be tried, and plains techniques can even destroy a demon by crystallizing it into stone.

The plains peoples live among demons twenty feet tall and greatly need witches, whom they call Inspirers. Inspirers bear tattoos of Inspiration on their faces, are guarded by ritual servants who also keep clan secrets from outsiders, and answer to a head Inspirer. The clans care only how well someone deals with demons, not where they come from.
